chapters.title: AI Documents
chapters.subtitle: Ask about a file in a chat

steps.text: Sometimes the answer is in a file. This video shows how a person attaches a document to a chat, how the assistant answers from it, and how it can read the charts inside it. It also shows the settings that control it.
A person has a file and a question: a policy, a report, a contract. They should not wait for an administrator to add it to the assistant.
With attachments on, the person attaches the file to the chat and asks. The assistant reads it, and answers from it.
The file belongs to that chat only. It never becomes part of the knowledge of the profile, and other people never see it.
Text, Markdown, JSON, XML, HTML, YAML and log files, spreadsheets, and PDF, Word and PowerPoint files, when those features are on.
A document is read, split into passages, and searched by meaning. A very long document is refused, rather than stored where it cannot be searched.

Charts and pictures inside a document can be described by a vision model, so that the assistant can answer about them. A figure is worth describing when it has a caption, or when the text refers to it.
Open Settings, Artificial Intelligence, and find the Documents section. The Index profile is the documents index that stores every attachment. Once people use it, avoid switching to another one.
Document retrieval mode is the site default. Chunk gives the assistant only the matching passages. Hierarchical gives it the whole documents they come from.
Allow document uploads in chat interactions and Allow image uploads in chat interactions turn attachments on or off for the Chat Interactions screen. Pictures need a vision deployment.
Largest document that can be indexed is the most characters of text one document may have. Zero means no limit.
Describe figures in uploaded documents decides whether charts and pictures are described. It uses a vision model and costs more, so it is the expensive part of an upload.
The vision model is the Default vision deployment, in the Deployments section of the same page. Without one, nothing is described.
Attachments are allowed profile by profile. Open the profile, open the Knowledge tab, and tick Allow session document uploads.
Describe figures in uploaded documents follows the site default, or you choose for this profile. Choose Describe figures, and click Save.
Open a chat with the profile. An Attach files button appears, with the list of formats that it accepts.
Click Attach files, and choose the file. Here it is the return policy of a company.
Then ask something that only the file answers: can I return opened software?
The assistant answers from the file: no, opened software cannot be returned.
Now a P.D.F. report with a chart. The sales numbers are only in the chart. The chart has a caption, Figure one, which is how the site knows it matters. Attach it the same way.
Ask: which quarter sold the most units?
The assistant read the chart, and answers from it: the third quarter. Describing a figure takes a little longer, which is why an attachment with figures is slower to prepare.
A policy or a contract: ask what it says about one clause, instead of reading all of it.
A report with charts: ask for the highest, the lowest or the trend.
A specification: ask the assistant to compare it with another file in the same chat.
Choose the documents index, allow attachments on a profile, and let people ask about their own files, charts included. Thanks for watching.
